name: Blue-Violet Black
lede: Blue-Violet Black is a very dark, nearly neutral grey with a faint cool cast, a shade of black rather than of blue.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The name comes from Ridgway's 1912 color atlas, where very dark blacks are tilted slightly toward a hue, and the later ISCC-NBS system kept it at block 187 [1]. The swatch is almost neutral and sits close to charcoal grey [1]. The name itself comes from the atlas's scheme, not from any pigment [1].

The books we hold have nothing on this exact color. They do show that black was long placed at the far end of the old order of colors, after violet, in the sequence white, yellow, orange, red, green, blue, violet, black [3]. That sequence dominated thinking from the fourth century BCE to the seventeenth century CE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Blue-Violet Black appears in 2.22% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1900s at 3.2% of that century's paintings, 2.6 times the baseline [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a shadow, in 39% of cases [2]. Its most devoted painter is Henri Matisse, in 5 of 50 works here [2]. Dark pigments and varnish shift in photographs, so these are looks, not recipes [2].

origin.named_after: Ridgway's tilted blacks; origin undocumented beyond the atlas
